page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-threaded and multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. Tradeoffs are evident in multi-threaded decompression and software compilation, which score in the bottom 25% tier. Static web serving throughput is also limited, registering in the bottom 25% tier.

With its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier single-core execution speed, this server class offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization. It is suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and text processing tasks. It is less suitable for highly parallelized compute tasks, large-scale software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where its limited core count and lower multi-threaded benchmark scores present performance bottlenecks.
